name: Monday Night Mayhem (Dec.18/97)

name: "January 1st" Show (4 Jan 1998)

matches.how: Bowa the Snake Man pinned champion Dark Justice after an unaffiliated 'Ultimate' Mike Mitchells climbed from the crowd and missile dropkicked Justice from behind.
The Maltese Falcon won by disqualification when the Perfect Role Models ran in for a five-on-one beatdown after Falcon slapped the fourth turnbuckle.

Mustafa was awarded the title after Arain of the Perfect Role Models, installed as acting replacement referee when senior referee Willie Feldman was knocked out, ruled the pinfall his way; commentary called the decision controversial.
Champion Dave Diamond retained by pinfall over Amoral after a bulldog onto the title belt he had thrown to the outside.

notes: The delayed broadcast of NPWA's own New Year's card (an in-fiction cold open blames 'production flaks' for the four-day delay from a planned 1 January air date). Two title changes: Bowa the Snake Man wins the Television Championship from Dark Justice, and Mustafa regains the North American Championship from The Cougar in a contested finish. 'Ultimate' Mike Mitchells debuts as a new Perfect Role Model after his ringside interference. Also on the card: Tyr the Nightmare defeats 'El Techno Kid' David Fulton; Trace Michaels and his valet Mora Cox preview the coming Cruiserweight tournament; the returning masked villains Locutus and Arnold Hawkins hunt an NPWA official called the Sheik; Resident Evil (Blade and Jack Hammer, managed by Tank) preview a Valentine's Day Massacre tag title challenge against champions Drama.

name: Mayhem (12 Jan 1998)

matches.how: Non-title 'Champion vs Champion' main event: World Champion Dave Diamond pins North American Champion Mustafa with the Hollywood Death Drop after a distraction from 'The Demon' Damien Lestat.
matches.note: No title changed hands; a non-title match between the two reigning champions.

notes: The debut episode of NPWA Mayhem, the promotion's new Sunday supershow. First-round Cruiserweight Championship tournament matches open the new title's own bracket; The Siberian Express (Ivan Drago and Andrei Bolotov) debut as a tag team, defeating an opponent ('Wyldside') this pass does not mint. No NPWA title changes hands.

name: Mayhem (18 Jan 1998)

matches.how: Major Victory pins champion Mustafa with the Americannon shoulderblock after Gan Green trips Mustafa outside the ring.

No clear finish reaches the page: an unaffiliated 'Johnny Johnston' interferes with a chair, powerbombing and finishing Glitter Boy with a Half-Nelson DDT before the referee can make a count; the Television Championship does not change hands on this pass's own reading.
matches.note: No winner_side recorded; the broadcast does not show a decision.

matches.how: Dark Justice defeats new Perfect Role Model Atticus Payne, standing in for an absent Gan Green.

notes: North American Championship changes hands: Major Victory defeats Mustafa. A new Perfect Role Model, Atticus Payne, wrestles his first match for the group. The Television Championship match between champion Bowa the Snake Man and the previously-undefeated Glitter Boy is broken up by outside interference from an unaffiliated 'Johnny Johnston' before any fall; the title does not change hands on the evidence this pass read. Also on the card: The Fear Machine (Black Sarah, Justin Cross and Michael Monroe) battle Cold Death to a double count-out draw.

name: Attention Women's E-Wrestling Fans! (20 Jan 1998)
notes: Registered as a document (not a card) for holdings discoverability: an out-of-character recruitment call announcing plans to launch an NPWA Women's Division, naming the existing NPWA Tag Team Division Head as a reference point for the role and previewing the tournament that opens on Mayhem later in 1998.

name: NPWA Disaster Area (14 May 1998)
notes: A magazine-format recap/interview show (not a live card): the reigning World Heavyweight Champion "The Wrecker" Mick McGreggor cuts a promo declining a title shot to Chris King and Doc Toxic, then accepts a challenge from El Jobbo Grande; Locutus interviewed on his Sole Survivor plans; the Fear Machine (Justin Cross & Michael Monroe) cut promos ahead of a six-man tag; a Wrestling Relics segment replays a 1996 ladder match between since-retired wrestlers Jack Butler and Jonathan Shock; upcoming Sole Survivor '98 card previewed (a 30-man battle royale, a Crown of Thorns match for McGreggor's title against Damien Lestat, a Taipei Death Match).

name: Mayhem (18 May 1998)

matches.note: retained; made Dark Justice submit to the Kalamazoo Clutch

notes: Also on the card: a first-round Women's Championship tournament match (Anne Arky d. Rekka Sakura); a six-man tag pitting Shaz, Blade & Pineapple (Juicy Fruits) against Justin Cross, "Senator" Carthy McJoseph & The Executioner; a non-title Cruiserweight match ("Hot Shot" Jet Mini d. Atticus Payne by disqualification, Payne billed the undefeated champion who rarely defends); a Damien Lestat promo teasing an NPWA Championship Committee grievance.

name: Mayhem (25 May 1998)

matches.note: retained by disqualification after Damien Lestat interfered with a taser, fork and knife; Valtharius the Mad (rspwf-tagged, unminted tenure) also attacked McGreggor's bodyguard, The Man They Call Nug

notes: Also on the card: Mustafa pins Sebastian Jericho for the Television Title (an angle, not shown as a formal defense) is teased for a future show; a card of upcoming matches is announced for the following week including tag, North American and Cruiserweight title bouts. Both a Cruiserweight semifinal (Ryan Winters d. Jose Chavez) and a full undercard of squash matches are named but not detailed here.

name: Mayhem (29 Sep 1998)

matches.note: won his first defense over Mike Mitchells (unminted) with the Caffeine Crashdown
retained (Ratings Buster) over The Kaiser (unminted) after a mass ringside brawl involving Valtharius the Mad, the Cadaver Connection and the Glitter Boy

matches.stipulation: Coal Miner's Glove triangle match for the NPWA Millennium Championship
matches.note: Sampson pinned champion Randy Gant using a second glove planted by Locutus Grew out of a chaotic Locutus-Dark Justice Millennium Division qualifier interrupted by Gant and Sampson; the referee restarted it as a three-way with Gant's title on the line.
the Outcast Rogues won when Arion pinned Blade after a jumped restart (a referee swap by the Asian Revolution/Rogues' allies was overturned)

notes: Also featured: a 12-man tag announced for the following week (Mustafa, the Silent Striker, Justin van Drake, Will Geddings, Atticus Payne & Bowa the Snake Man vs. Mick McGreggor & the Perfect Role Models) after a post-match riot; Gan Green's paranoid belief a vampire-gimmick wrestler elsewhere is 'stealing his identity,' used by McGreggor to recruit the Perfect Role Models into his own feud with Col. Mustafa.

name: Mayhem (6 Oct 1998)

matches.note: retained (result read from a subsequent show reference; card billed him defending)

matches.stipulation: NPWA North American Tag Team Championship
matches.note: The Cult (Doctor Death, with Locutus wrestling in Father Armageddon's place) retained a schoolboy-roll finish over the Larson Brothers (unminted)
retained (Ratings Buster) over The Glitter Boy (rspwf-tagged, unminted tenure) in a ladder match

retained by disqualification after "Untouchable" Randy Gant interfered against challenger Steve Sampson Sampson entered as reigning Millennium Champion; the DQ finish meant Toast kept the World Title and Sampson kept the Millennium belt.

notes: A satellite/production gag interrupts the show's own opening angle (Jolt fleeing Randy Gant in a Hum-V) and is never resolved on-air, per the show's own framing device.

name: Mayhem: 5th Anniversary Special (13 Oct 1998)

matches.stipulation: NPWA Cruiserweight Championship of the World
matches.note: retained with a Shooting Star Press over Doug Arnott (unminted)

matches.stipulation: NPWA North American Tag Team Championship
matches.note: Assault and Battery won; Tom Harris rolled up Locutus (wrestling for The Cult in Father Armageddon's place)
retained when Doc Toxic (rspwf-tagged, unminted tenure) pulled himself off a pin and walked out on his manager Karachel's orders, ruled a countout

matches.stipulation: Double Jeopardy six-man match: if a member of Toast's team is pinned, the Glitter Boy becomes World Champion and the Rogues keep the World Tag belts; if a member of the Rogues' team is pinned, the Asian Revolution become World Tag Champions and Toast keeps his World Title
matches.note: Jo Ozawa pinned the Glitter Boy, crowning the Asian Revolution and keeping Toast's title safe A third man, the Glitter Boy (unminted, billed the number-one WHC contender), fought alongside the Rogues under a Double Jeopardy stipulation naming him personally (pin a member of Toast's team, become World Champion) -- he is carried in this match's stipulation/how text rather than in sides[], per the unminted-opponent convention. The Asian Revolution briefly offered the belts back to the Rogues after winning, then attacked them and kept the titles.

notes: A milestone card marking the promotion's own fifth anniversary, corroborating the wing's existing 1993 founding date; also features a mask-vs-mask match (The Silent Striker defeats The Coroner (unminted) for possession of Doc Toxic's mask) and multiple guest-commentary segments.

name: Hell On Earth (1 Nov 1998)

matches.stipulation: NPWA North American Tag Team Championship, double steel-cage match
matches.note: the Masters of Disaster won when a masked interloper struck Eddie Simpson with brass knuckles moments before Jack Hammer covered him

notes: "Breakfast" Bobby Toast is confirmed still NPWA World Heavyweight Champion at this show's close. The identity of the masked interloper who cost Assault and Battery the North American Tag belts is left unresolved in the held record.
